submitted_fields.style: Instrumental buoyant breakbeat electronica, 126 BPM, 4/4 in D minor, around 3:30. Begin with four bars of rubbery mono bass playing a plain two-note rhythm; add chopped live break drums and a light ride, then a soft pulse-keyboard hook, with tremolo guitar holding quiet chords later. Target Dm - G - C, held for two, one and one bars; the G chord gives a hopeful Dorian color. The game-like lead uses just two short pitches with space, repeating the same figure throughout. Guitar supports harmony without a second melody. Bright forward motion with a wistful edge. In the middle remove guitar and keyboard for a short bass-and-drums passage, then return the identical hook in warmer harmony. Change weight and space rather than adding runs; finish with a clean compact stop.

submitted_fields.style: Instrumental bright chip breakbeat, 124 BPM, 4/4 in B major, around 3:20. Open with two bars of light hats and dry rim clicks, then a crisp square-wave hook; a short sub bass and thin poly-synth chords join separately. Target B - D# - G#m, two bars on B and one on each following chord. Keep the main hook to two evenly spaced pitches with a rest, exactly the same simple rhythm on each return. Springy two-step drums give lift without frantic lead playing. Warm, sunny and lightly nostalgic rather than deeply sad. Chords open in the refrain; a two-bar stop leaves only the tiny hook before the groove returns. Keep the same game-console lead at the final brighter refrain; no answering arpeggio or extra lead. Use rhythmic gaps and wider harmony for growth, then resolve quietly.

Add a muted synth bass, then warm analog chord beds; loose electronic break drums with a short gated snare arrive later. Target F#m - D - A - E, two bars per chord once harmony begins. Withdraw one layer at a time in the middle, briefly exposing the original pair of notes. The same figure returns over fuller chords and drums. Sad but gently luminous; let repetition and texture carry emotion rather than decorative runs.

submitted_fields.style: Instrumental bright yet aching digital electronica, 125 BPM, 4/4 in E major, around four minutes. Start with the main hook immediately: just two soft keyboard notes and a long rest, played alone for four bars. Rounded bass follows, then a straight hybrid big beat with wide acoustic snare; clean guitar joins as long held chords. Target E - A - Am - E, two bars per chord after the bare opening. The plain 8-bit/16-bit keyboard remains the only lead throughout. Guitar adds harmonic width without a riff or countermelody. Keep the same tiny hook unchanged as the beat becomes exhilarating and the minor-color chord adds longing. A brief middle break leaves the keyboard and guitar, then all layers return for one warm final refrain. Fullness comes from chord voicing and rhythmic force, never more melody notes. End with the hook alone.
submitted_fields.exclude: vocals, audience noise, busy lead or bass runs, long sixteenth-note arpeggios, competing countermelodies, comic arcade effects, festival drops
